note: Re-judged after a02374d9ad changed TestRFC2516HostStopsUsingTheSessionWhenLCPTerminates against RFC 2516 Section 7 ("When LCP terminates, the Host and Access concentrator MUST stop using that PPPoE session."). The only change: the post-termination sendEchoReply result, previously discarded, must now satisfy errors.Is(err, io.ErrClosedPipe). That error is produced only by sessionLink.Write's closed guard (dialer.go), passed through writeClientPacket unwrapped and by sendEchoReply with %w, so the check pins the session's own refusal; the hostChannel still accepts writes after Close, so neither this nor the zero-later-frames check can pass unless superviseNetworkPhase closed the link after keepaliveLoop returned on the Terminate-Request. Every earlier assertion is kept (exactly one Terminate-Ack for Identifier 5, one channel close, Done published, link.Write refused, no frame after the Ack): strictly stronger. Negative TestRFC2516HostKeepsTheSessionUntilLCPTerminates unchanged: Echo-Request and stray Terminate-Ack leave Done open and the Host answering, only the Terminate-Request ends it, so the stop is tied to LCP termination. AC half unchanged: handleSessionDown removes the session and sends its PADT (exact CODE, SESSION_ID, destination MAC); an unknown SID sends nothing and removes nothing. Discrimination records (re-taken 45025b3639) replace whole producer bodies with a panic, which proves only that the units reach the producers; the specific break (dropping link.Close from superviseNetworkPhase) was judged by reading: it leaves link.stopped open and Write succeeding, so three assertions go red.
